mainTopic: A shapeless corpse and טומאת אהל; when a miscarried limb or a partial birth counts as לידה; and the birth and impurity rules for a טומטום and אנדרוגינוס.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the debate about a corpse that lost its shape: the גמרא turns ריש לקיש's proof from the burned-corpse ברייתא around, and רבינא shows that רבי יוחנן's view matches רבי אליעזר on the ashes of burned bodies. אביי, רבא and רבינא then explain how a burned body can still keep its frame. Next, a ברייתא rules that a woman who miscarries a shaped hand or foot is טמאה לידה. רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא add that she gets no ימי טוהר, since the main birth may have been long before, and אביי defends this against רב יוסף's challenge. רב הונא rules that a fetus that put out its hand and pulled it back makes the mother impure. After challenges, the גמרא concludes this is only מדרבנן and the פסוק about תמר is an אסמכתא. A new משנה teaches the rules for miscarrying a טומטום or אנדרוגינוס, alone or as a twin, and when a baby counts as born. The גמרא explains why the twin-with-a-boy case was needed. The amud ends with רב's ruling on a טומטום or אנדרוגינוס who sees white or red discharge, and the פסוק behind it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Restating the inference from the burned-corpse ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא (small doorways stay pure) and restates ריש לקיש's inference: the large doorways are impure only because the frame is intact, so a shapeless corpse would make nothing impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: They declared the small doorways pure. And you inferred from this: the reason the large doorways are impure is that the frame is intact, so if it were not intact, everything would be pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the end of the ברייתא and spells out ריש לקיש's reasoning from it. It is setting this up so it can reject it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא makes the large doorways impure because the corpse will eventually be carried out through one of them. ריש לקיש focused on the words 'its frame is intact' and concluded that a corpse without its shape would not spread טומאה at all. This is the reasoning about to be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: Its frame/skeleton remains intact; the body still has its shape
Small doorways, less than four טפחים wide, too narrow to carry a whole body through
You made an inference from it (reading what the text implies)
But if it were not so (the reverse case)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא did not say the case of a shapeless corpse is pure. That 'otherwise it is pure' is only ריש לקיש's inference, and the next step challenges it.

phrases.english: But they declared the small doorways pure for it.
phrases.notes: This is the end of the ברייתא quoted just before: when the frame is intact, the large doorways are impure.

phrases.english: And you inferred from it:
The reason is that its frame is intact,
but if not so, it is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up ריש לקיש's proof from the previous section, restating it before rejecting it.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's position that a corpse that lost its shape does not spread טומאת אהל
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a burned corpse whose frame remains: large doorways impure, small doorways pure

steps.title: Reversing the inference: without the frame, even small doorways are impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the ברייתא the opposite way: the small doorways are pure only because the frame is intact. Without it, every small doorway would be impure, since the body could be taken out one limb at a time.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, infer it the other way: only because the frame is intact are the small doorways pure. Otherwise the small doorways would also be impure, because each one is fit for taking out the body limb by limb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down ריש לקיש's proof by showing that the 'frame is intact' detail actually points the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An intact body can only leave through a large doorway, so only the large doorways are impure. A body that has fallen apart can be carried out limb by limb through any small doorway, so every doorway would become impure. The intact frame makes the ruling milder, not stricter, so no proof comes from here that a shapeless corpse is pure.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; the opposite is true
In this direction; the other way
Is fit for taking out
A limb

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא proves nothing for ריש לקיש. Read correctly, it suggests a shapeless corpse is even stricter, because its parts can pass through small doorways.
steps.whyThisMatters: This removes ריש לקיש's main proof and leaves רבי יוחנן's view (a corpse that lost its shape still spreads טומאה) standing.

phrases.english: On the contrary, infer from it in this direction:
It is because its frame is intact
that they declared the small doorways pure,
but if not so,
the small doorways are also impure,
because each and every one is fit
for taking out one limb at a time!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference restated in step 1 by reversing it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the entire proof ריש לקיש drew from the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The intact frame explains why the small doorways are pure, not why the large ones are impure. Without the frame, more doorways would be impure, not fewer.

steps.title: Which תנא agrees with רבי יוחנן?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי which earlier authority holds like רבי יוחנן, that a shapeless corpse still spreads טומאת אהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: whose opinion does רבי יוחנן follow?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא asks for an earlier source that matches רבי יוחנן's view. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that ריש לקיש's proof is gone, רבינא wants to anchor רבי יוחנן's ruling in a תנא from the משנה. Finding a תנא who agrees gives the view a solid basis.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? Which authority does this follow?

phrases.english: רבינא said to רב אשי:
רבי יוחנן, who said this, follows whom?
phrases.notes: This is about רבי יוחנן's ruling that a corpse that lost its shape still spreads טומאה under a roof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבי יוחנן, the גמרא now looks for a תנא who supports him.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a corpse without its shape still spreads טומאת אהל

steps.title: רבי יוחנן follows רבי אליעזר on the ashes of burned bodies
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that רבי יוחנן follows רבי אליעזר, who rules that the ashes of burned corpses spread טומאה when there is a רובע (a quarter of a קב).
steps.simpleTranslation: Like רבי אליעזר, as we learned in a משנה: regarding the ashes of burned bodies, רבי אליעזר says their measure is a quarter of a קב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings a משנה where רבי אליעזר treats ashes, which have no human shape at all, as able to make things impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ashes are the most extreme case of a corpse that lost its shape. If רבי אליעזר says a רובע of ashes spreads טומאה, he clearly holds that losing the shape does not cancel טומאה, which is exactly רבי יוחנן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Ashes of burned bodies
The minimum amount needed for a law to apply
A quarter of a קב, a measure of volume

phrases.english: Like רבי אליעזר, as we learned in a משנה:
The ashes of burned bodies:
רבי אליעזר says:
Their measure is a quarter of a קב.
phrases.notes: Meaning this much ash is enough to make things under the same roof impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question from step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן follows רבי אליעזר, who holds that ashes of burned bodies spread טומאה in the amount of a רובע

steps.title: How can a burned corpse keep its frame?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא means by a corpse that was burned yet kept its frame, since burning usually destroys the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of a corpse that was burned and its frame is still intact?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא's case and asks how it could really happen. This sets up the three answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning normally turns a body to ash, so a burned body with its shape still intact sounds like a contradiction. The גמרא wants a realistic picture of the case.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? What does the case look like?
A corpse that was burned

phrases.english: What is the case of
a corpse that was burned and its frame is intact?
phrases.notes: This is the case from the ברייתא in steps 1 and 2.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי מֵת שֶׁנִּשְׂרַף וְשִׁלְדּוֹ קַיֶּימֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי אליעזר discussion and returns to define the ברייתא's case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A realistic situation where a corpse is burned but keeps its shape

steps.title: Three answers: אביי, רבא and רבינא
steps.stepSummary: אביי says it was burned on a hard leather mat, רבא says on a marble slab, and רבינא says it was only scorched, not reduced to ash.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: for example, it was burned on top of a leather mat. רבא said: for example, it was burned on top of a marble slab. רבינא said: for example, it was only scorched.
steps.whatsHappening: Three אמוראים each describe a case where a burned body could still keep its shape.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי and רבא describe a surface underneath that does not burn and holds the remains in their shape, a leather mat or a marble slab. רבינא gives a simpler case: the body was only charred on the outside and never turned to ash.

keyTerms.meaning: A hard leather mat or spread that does not burn easily
A marble slab
Was scorched or charred
For example; such as a case where

steps.whatToRemember: A 'burned corpse whose frame is intact' is a body that still has its shape: burned on a surface that holds it together (אביי, רבא), or only scorched (רבינא).

phrases.english: אביי said:
For example, where he burned it on top of a leather mat.
רבא said:
For example, where he burned it on top of a marble slab.
רבינא said:
For example, where it was only scorched.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כְּגוֹן שֶׁשְּׂרָפוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי קַטְבֻלְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 with three different cases.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Burned on a leather mat (אביי), on a marble slab (רבא), or only scorched (רבינא)

steps.title: A miscarried shaped hand or foot makes the mother impure from childbirth
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a woman who miscarries a shaped hand or foot is טמאה לידה. We do not worry that it came from a גוף אטום.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: If a woman miscarries a shaped hand or a shaped foot, the mother has childbirth impurity. We do not worry that these limbs came from a fetus with a sealed body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא about a woman who miscarries only a hand or a foot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A limb alone is not a full birth, but most fetuses are normal. So we assume the limb came from a whole fetus and treat her as a woman who gave birth. We ignore the small chance that it came from a deformed גוף אטום, which would not count as a birth.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who miscarries
Shaped, with the fingers or toes clearly formed
Impure with the impurity of a woman after childbirth
A 'sealed' fetus body, one that is not properly formed and does not count as a birth
We are not concerned about that possibility

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A woman who miscarries a shaped hand
phrases.notes: חתוכה literally means 'cut.' Here it means the hand is fully formed, with its fingers clearly marked.

phrases.english: or a shaped foot —
its mother is impure with childbirth impurity,
and we are not concerned
that perhaps they came from a sealed body.
phrases.notes: A 'sealed body' is a badly formed fetus. If the limb came from one, it would not count as a birth at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, separate from the corpse and טומאת אהל discussion in steps 2-6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A miscarried shaped hand or foot makes the mother טמאה לידה. We assume it came from a normal fetus, not a גוף אטום.

steps.title: She gets no days of purity, because the birth may have been long ago
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא rule that this woman does not get ימי טוהר. The reason is that the main body may have come out much earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא both say: We do not give her days of purity. Why? Say that her birth was long ago.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים add a limit to the ברייתא: she keeps the impurity of childbirth, but she does not get the pure days that usually follow it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A birth is counted from when most of the fetus comes out. The hand or foot might have come out long after the main body. If so, her ימי טוהר may already be over, so we cannot let her treat blood now as pure.

keyTerms.meaning: Days of purity after childbirth impurity, when blood she sees does not make her impure
What is the reason?
Her birth was distant, meaning the main birth happened long before

steps.confusionAlert: She is still טמאה לידה. The אמוראים only take away the pure days after it, not the impurity.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: Rav Chisda and Rabba bar Rav Huna
both say:
We do not give her days of purity.
What is the reason?
Say that her birth was long ago.
phrases.notes: In other words, most of the fetus may have come out earlier, and this limb only came out now.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא דְּאָמְרִי תַרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ברייתא of step 7: childbirth impurity applies, but ימי טוהר do not.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who miscarries a lone limb does not get ימי טוהר, because the main birth may have happened long before.

steps.title: רב יוסף objects: the משנה should then add נדה strictures
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף cites a משנה about a miscarriage of unknown kind, which says she keeps the rules for a boy and a girl. If we always worry the birth was long ago, the משנה should also say she keeps the rules of a נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objects: 'A woman who miscarries, and it is not known what she miscarried, keeps the rules for a male and for a female.' If you think that in every case like this we say the birth was long ago, let the משנה also teach 'and for a נדה'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges step 8 with a משנה about a doubtful miscarriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that משנה the item could also be a limb from an earlier birth. By the logic of step 8, she would lose her ימי טוהר and have to treat blood like a נדה. The משנה mentions only male and female, so it seems not to worry that the birth was long ago.

keyTerms.meaning: She keeps the stricter rules of both a boy birth and a girl birth
If it enters your mind, meaning 'if you really think so'
A menstruating woman, for whom any blood makes her impure

phrases.english: Rav Yosef objects:
A woman who miscarries, and it is not known what she miscarried,
shall keep the rules for a male and for a female,
and if it enters your mind
that in every case like this
we say her birth was long ago,
let it teach 'and for a נדה' too!
phrases.notes: He means she would have no pure days, so any blood would make her impure like a נדה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning of step 8 from a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reasoning of רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא, הרחיקה לידתה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If we worry the birth was long ago, the משנה about an unknown miscarriage should add נדה strictures. Since it doesn't, the משנה seems not to share that worry.

steps.title: אביי: the משנה left out נדה to teach that her offering is eaten
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the משנה avoided mentioning נדה on purpose. Otherwise we might think her קרבן is brought but not eaten, and the משנה wants to teach that it is eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: If the משנה had taught 'for a נדה,' I would have thought she brings an offering but it is not eaten. So it teaches us that it is eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends step 8 by explaining why the משנה does not mention נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'נדה' might suggest we doubt she gave birth at all. Then her bird חטאת would be brought only out of doubt and could not be eaten. By leaving it out, the משנה shows she surely gave birth. The only doubt is when, so the worry that the birth was long ago still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first assumption)
The offering a woman brings after childbirth
It is not eaten, by the כהנים
It teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: A lone shaped limb makes her טמאה לידה but gives her no ימי טוהר, since the birth may have been long ago. The משנה leaves out נדה only to show that her קרבן is still eaten.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
If it had taught 'for a נדה,'
I would have said
she brings an offering but it is not eaten,
phrases.notes: The worry is that we doubt she gave birth at all, so the bird חטאת would be brought only because of the doubt.

phrases.english: so it teaches us that it is eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's objection in step 9 and protects the ruling of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the משנה left out a ruling: leaving it out teaches a different point.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning נדה would suggest we doubt she gave birth at all, so her קרבן would not be eaten.
steps.terutzMaskana: She surely gave birth, so her קרבן is eaten. The only doubt is when she gave birth, so the worry that the birth was long ago still applies.

steps.title: A fetus that put out its hand and pulled it back
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that if a fetus put its hand out and pulled it back, the mother is טמאה לידה. He brings a פסוק from the birth of תמר's twins.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: If a fetus put its hand out and then pulled it back in, its mother is impure as a woman who gave birth. As it says: 'And it happened, when she gave birth, that one put out a hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רב הונא: a hand coming out counts as a birth for טומאת לידה, even if the hand goes back in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a birth means the baby actually comes out. רב הונא says that just a hand coming out is enough to make the mother טמאה לידה. His proof is that the תורה calls the hand coming out of תמר's twin 'when she gave birth', even though that hand went back in.

keyTerms.meaning: A fetus, a baby still inside the mother
Put out its hand
And pulled it back in
Impure with the impurity of a woman who gave birth

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
If a fetus put out its hand and pulled it back in,
its mother is impure as a woman who gave birth,
as it says: 'And it happened when she gave birth, that one put out a hand.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about a partial birth, after the earlier discussion of miscarried limbs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fetus putting out its hand, even if it pulls it back, makes the mother טמאה לידה, based on the פסוק about תמר.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the mother need not worry at all
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה challenges רב הונא from a ברייתא. It says that if a fetus put out its hand, the mother need not worry about anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה challenged: 'If a fetus put out its hand, its mother does not need to worry about anything!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה quotes a ברייתא that seems to say the exact opposite of רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said a hand coming out makes the mother טמאה לידה. The ברייתא says that in this same case the mother does not need to worry 'about anything'. That sounds like there is no birth here at all.

keyTerms.meaning: She needs to worry, she must be careful about it
About anything at all

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda raised an objection:
If a fetus put out its hand,
its mother does not need to worry about anything!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב הונא's ruling from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that a hand coming out makes the mother טמאה לידה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about the very same case says the mother need not be concerned about anything, so it seems there is no birth at all.

steps.title: רב נחמן explains what רב הונא really meant
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says רב הונא told him personally what he meant. The mother must be strict, but she gets no ימי טוהר until most of the baby comes out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: It was explained to me by רב הונא himself. She does have to be concerned. But we do not give her days of purity until most of the baby comes out.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends רב הונא by explaining the limits of his ruling. The mother keeps the strict side of the rule but gets none of its leniencies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman after birth has a strict side, the days of טומאה, and a lenient side, the ימי טוהר when blood she sees is pure. רב נחמן says רב הונא only meant the strict side. The lenient ימי טוהר come only once most of the baby is out. This begins to soften the clash with the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: It was explained to me personally
As for being concerned, she must be concerned
Days of purity after birth, when blood she sees is pure
Most of it, here most of the baby

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:

phrases.aramaic: לְדִידִי מִיפָּרְשָׁא לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: It was explained to me personally by Rav Huna himself:
as for being concerned, she must be concerned,
but we do not give her days of purity
until most of it comes out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: לְדִידִי מִיפָּרְשָׁא לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יהודה's challenge in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ruling: only the strict side applies, not the leniency.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא seemed to treat the hand as a full birth, which clashes with the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The mother keeps the strictures of birth, but gets ימי טוהר only after most of the baby comes out.

steps.title: But the ברייתא says 'not about anything'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. The ברייתא says she need not worry about anything at all, so how can she have to be strict?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא says 'its mother does not need to worry about anything'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presses on the exact words of the ברייתא. רב נחמן's answer still does not seem to fit them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said the mother must still be strict. The ברייתא says she need not worry 'about anything', which seems to rule out even being strict. So the clash with the ברייתא is not solved yet.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, used to start a challenge
It says

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אֵין ״אִמּוֹ חוֹשֶׁשֶׁת לְכׇל דָּבָר״ קָאָמַר!
phrases.english: But it says, 'its mother does not need to worry about anything'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אֵין אִמּוֹ חוֹשֶׁשֶׁת לְכׇל דָּבָר קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's answer in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that the mother must still be strict.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's words 'not about anything' seem to rule out any concern at all, even a strict one.

steps.title: No concern from the תורה, but concern from the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the ברייתא means the mother need not worry מדאורייתא. מדרבנן she must still be strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: She does not need to worry about anything according to תורה law. But according to rabbinic law, she must be concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי settles the clash by saying the ברייתא and רב הונא are talking about two different levels of law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's 'not about anything' is about the תורה level: from the תורה, a hand alone is not a birth. רב הונא's strictness is a rule of the רבנן. So both statements are true, each on its own level.

keyTerms.meaning: According to תורה law
According to rabbinic law, a rule set by the חכמים

steps.confusionAlert: Now רב הונא's rule is only מדרבנן. The ברייתא's 'not about anything' means only that the תורה does not count a hand as a birth.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
She does not need to worry about anything by Torah law,
but by rabbinic law she must be concerned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אֵינָהּ חוֹשֶׁשֶׁת לְכׇל דָּבָר מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא's wording in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting levels of law: תורה law versus rabbinic law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to deny any concern at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: From the תורה there is no concern, but the רבנן require her to be strict.

steps.title: But רב הונא brought a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the rule is only מדרבנן, why did רב הונא prove it from a פסוק?
steps.simpleTranslation: But he quoted a verse!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's answer by pointing to the פסוק רב הונא brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A proof from a פסוק sounds like a תורה law. That clashes with אביי's claim that רב הונא's rule is only rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק, a verse

phrases.english: But he quoted a verse?
phrases.notes: This points back to רב הונא's proof from תמר's twins at the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that רב הונא's rule is only rabbinic.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב הונא brought a פסוק as proof, which suggests a תורה-level rule.

steps.title: The פסוק is only a hint
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the rule really is מדרבנן. The פסוק is only an אסמכתא, a hint to lean the rule on.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is rabbinic law, and the verse is just a support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק is not a real source. It is only a hint attached to a rabbinic rule. This closes the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אסמכתא is a פסוק the חכמים point to as a hint for their own rule, not as its true source. So רב הונא can quote a פסוק and the rule can still be only מדרבנן. With this, רב הונא's rule, the ברייתא and the פסוק all fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק used as a hint or support for a rabbinic rule, not its real source
Merely, just

steps.whatToRemember: If a fetus put out its hand and pulled it back: from the תורה this is not a birth. מדרבנן the mother keeps the strictures of birth, but gets no ימי טוהר until most of the baby comes out. The פסוק about תמר is only an אסמכתא.

phrases.english: It is by rabbinic law, and the verse is just a support.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16 and closes the topic.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recasting the source: the פסוק is an אסמכתא, not a real source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Quoting a פסוק seemed to show the rule comes from the תורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule is rabbinic, and the פסוק only serves as a hint.

steps.title: New משנה: miscarrying a טומטום or an אנדרוגינוס
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that a woman who miscarries a טומטום or an אנדרוגינוס keeps the rules of both a boy and a girl.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A woman who miscarries a טומטום or an אנדרוגינוס must keep the rules for a boy and for a girl.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new משנה about a birth where we cannot tell for sure whether the baby is a boy or a girl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A boy and a girl have different time periods of טומאה and טהרה after birth. Since this baby's gender is in doubt, she keeps the stricter side of each. She is impure for fourteen days, as for a girl, and her ימי טוהר end at forty days, as for a boy.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
A woman who miscarries or gives birth
A baby whose sex organs are covered, so its gender is unknown
A baby with both male and female sex organs
She keeps the rules of both a boy and a girl

phrases.english: Mishnah:
A woman who miscarries a tumtum or a hermaphrodite
shall keep the rules for a male and for a female.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the end of the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who miscarries a טומטום or אנדרוגינוס keeps the stricter rules of both a boy and a girl.

steps.title: Twins: A Doubtful Baby Together with a Boy or a Girl
steps.stepSummary: If a טומטום or אנדרוגינוס is born together with a boy, the mother keeps the rules of both a boy and a girl. If it is born together with a girl, she keeps only the rules of a girl.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the twins are a טומטום and a boy, or an אנדרוגינוס and a boy, she keeps the rules for a boy and for a girl. If the twins are a טומטום and a girl, or an אנדרוגינוס and a girl, she keeps only the rules for a girl.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps going with its ruling about a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס. Now it teaches what happens when one of them is born as a twin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a boy twin, the doubtful baby might be a girl, so the mother must also keep a girl's rules. With a girl twin, the girl's rules already apply for sure. A girl's days are longer and already cover a boy's days, so the doubtful twin adds nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: literally 'she shall sit'; she keeps the set days of impurity and purity after a birth
for a boy and for a girl; she keeps the stricter side of both
for a girl only

phrases.english: A tumtum and a male, a hermaphrodite and a male (as twins) —
she observes the rules of both a male and a female;
a tumtum and a female, a hermaphrodite and a female —
she observes the rules of a female alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the משנה's ruling on a single טומטום or אנדרוגינוס to the case of twins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Doubtful baby plus a boy: she keeps the rules of both. Doubtful baby plus a girl: she keeps only a girl's rules.

steps.title: When Does a Baby Count as Born?
steps.stepSummary: A baby that comes out in pieces or feet first counts as born once most of it is out. A baby that comes out head first counts as born once most of its head is out, which means the forehead.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the baby came out in pieces or feet first, it counts as born once most of it has come out. If it came out the normal way, it counts as born only once most of its head is out. What counts as most of its head? Once its forehead comes out.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new topic. It defines the exact moment a baby counts as born, so we know when the mother's birth rules start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two measures. For an unusual birth, in pieces or feet first, we need most of the body. For a normal head-first birth, most of the head is enough, and the forehead marks that point.

keyTerms.meaning: cut up; coming out in pieces
reversed; coming out feet first
like a baby that was born
the normal way, head first
its forehead

phrases.english: If it emerged in pieces, or reversed —
phrases.notes: 'Reversed' means feet first instead of head first.

phrases.english: once most of it emerges, it is like one born.
If it emerged in its usual way —
not until most of its head emerges.
And what is most of its head?
From when its forehead emerges.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling in the משנה on a separate topic: the moment of birth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pieces or feet first: born once most of the body is out. Head first: born once most of the head, the forehead, is out.

steps.title: Why Teach the Twin Case with a Boy?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה had to teach the twin case with a boy. A טומטום alone already makes her keep both sets of rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, a טומטום by itself or an אנדרוגינוס by itself already makes her keep the rules of a boy and a girl. Do we really need to be told this about a טומטום with a boy, or an אנדרוגינוס with a boy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה. It challenges the first half of the twin ruling as seemingly unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the doubtful baby alone already makes her keep both sets of rules, adding a boy twin changes nothing. So the twin-with-a-boy case seems like a repeat. The גמרא wants to know what new thing it teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: now; since we already know this
by itself, alone
is it needed? (it seems obvious)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Now, a tumtum by itself
and a hermaphrodite by itself
you said she observes the rules of a male and a female,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets, 'you said,' is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: is it necessary to say a tumtum and a male, a hermaphrodite and a male?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the twin ruling from step 19 and asks why it was needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling about a טומטום or אנדרוגינוס with a boy twin.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is a קל וחומר-style 'obvious' challenge. If the doubtful baby alone already makes her keep both sets of rules, a boy twin cannot change that.

steps.title: Twins Do Not Have to Be the Same
steps.stepSummary: The case was needed. Based on רבי יצחק, we might think twins must both be boys. The משנה teaches that both parents may have released seed at the same moment, making one twin a boy and the other a girl.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have said this: רבי יצחק taught that if the woman releases seed first, she has a boy, and if the man releases seed first, she has a girl. So since this twin is a boy, the other must be a boy too. The משנה teaches us otherwise. We can say both released seed at the same time, so this one is a boy and that one is a girl.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It explains the mistake the משנה is protecting us from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק's rule could suggest that twins from one act share one cause, so they must be the same. If so, a boy twin would prove the doubtful twin is a boy too. The משנה rejects this, because both parents may have released seed at once, so the twins can differ.

keyTerms.meaning: it was needed
you might have said (the mistaken first thought)
releases seed
this teaches us (the correct view)
at the same moment

steps.whatToRemember: The twin-with-a-boy ruling teaches that a boy twin does not prove the doubtful twin is a boy. Twins can be a boy and a girl, so the mother keeps both sets of rules.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יצחק's rule is not being rejected. The גמרא only shows that it does not force both twins to be the same, because both parents can release seed at once.

phrases.english: It was necessary; lest you say,
since Rabbi Yitzḥak said:
if the woman emits seed first, she gives birth to a male,
if the man emits seed first, she gives birth to a female,

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא מִדְּהַאי זָכָר — הַאי נָמֵי זָכָר?
phrases.english: I might say: since this one is a male, that one is also a male?
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the boy twin, and 'that one' is the טומטום or אנדרוגינוס.

phrases.english: It teaches us otherwise.
Say: both emitted seed at the same time,
so this one is a male and that one is a female.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21 by showing what the twin case adds.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: shows the extra case prevents a mistaken conclusion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Based on רבי יצחק, twins share one cause, so a boy twin proves the doubtful twin is a boy too, and she would keep only a boy's rules.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both parents may release seed at once, so the doubtful twin could be a girl, and she keeps the rules of both a boy and a girl.

steps.title: A single kind of discharge from a person of unclear gender
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes רב. If a טומטום or אנדרוגינוס sees white or red, they are not liable for entering the מקדש, and תרומה they touch is not burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רב: A טומטום or an אנדרוגינוס who saw a white discharge or a red discharge is not liable for entering the מקדש, and we do not burn תרומה because of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ruling from רב. It is about a person of unclear gender who has only one kind of discharge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A white discharge makes a man impure, and red blood makes a woman impure. Since we do not know whether this person is a man or a woman, one kind alone only makes them impure out of doubt. That doubt is not enough to make them liable for the מקדש, and it is not enough to burn תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: A person whose private parts are covered over, so we cannot tell if they are male or female
A person who has both male and female organs
White, meaning a white discharge like a man's זיבה
Red, meaning red blood like a woman's נדה blood
Entering the מקדש while impure
Burning תרומה that has definitely become impure

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rav said:
A tumtum and a hermaphrodite
who saw white or red
phrases.notes: White is the kind of discharge that makes a man impure. Red is the blood that makes a woman impure.

phrases.english: are not liable for entering the Temple,
and we do not burn the teruma on their account.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס. It follows the earlier steps that also dealt with them, but now the question is about their own impurity.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a טומטום or אנדרוגינוס sees only white or only red, their impurity is a doubt. They are not liable for entering the מקדש, and תרומה is not burned because of them.

steps.title: Both kinds of discharge together, and the start of the source
steps.stepSummary: If they see white and red together, תרומה is burned. They are still not liable for the מקדש, and רב begins quoting the פסוק that teaches this.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they saw white and red together, they are not liable for entering the מקדש, but we do burn תרומה because of them, as it says: "Both male and female..."
steps.whatsHappening: רב continues his ruling with a second case, where the person sees both kinds of discharge together. He then starts quoting a פסוק to explain the part about the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seeing both kinds together makes the person impure for sure. If they are a man, the white makes them impure, and if they are a woman, the red does. So the impurity is certain and תרומה is burned. But being impure for sure still does not make them liable for the מקדש, and the reason comes from the words "מזכר ועד נקבה", which are explained on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Together, at the same time
"Both male and female", the פסוק about sending impure people out of the camp
But, marking the difference between the מקדש rule and the תרומה rule

steps.confusionAlert: "Not liable" does not mean they are allowed to go into the מקדש. It only means they do not get the punishment or the קרבן that someone normally gets for entering while impure.
steps.whyThisMatters: This case shows that the two rules can split. Being certainly impure is enough to burn תרומה, but liability for the מקדש depends on the פסוק.

phrases.english: If they saw white and red together,
they are not liable for entering the Temple,
but we do burn the teruma on their account,
phrases.notes: Whether they are male or female, one of the two discharges makes them impure, so the impurity is certain.

phrases.english: as it is stated: "Both male and female
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:3. The quote continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב's ruling with a second case, where the impurity is certain. It begins giving a source for the מקדש part.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If they see white and red together, תרומה is burned because of them. They are still not liable for entering the מקדש, based on the פסוק "מזכר ועד נקבה".
